{
  "reviews": [
    {
      "benchmark": "arc",
      "instrument_review": "ARC-AGI-2 supports comparisons of performance on unfamiliar grid problems when exposure, evaluation conditions and benchmark versions are comparable. Its example-based tasks directly require producing outputs consistent with an inferred rule, but successful answers alone do not establish the reasoning process used. Human difficulty studies and removal of repeated rules support test construction; however, the human study covered a larger pool than the final benchmark, and matching human difficulty does not establish equivalent difficulty for AI systems. Scoring is explicit: exact matches earn credit per input, input scores are averaged within problems, and problem scores are then averaged. Consequently, the reported score can include partially solved problems while giving no credit for partially correct grids. Verified settings and spending limits help comparison, but a single run without repeatability estimates leaves small differences difficult to interpret. Public materials and revision records aid inspection, although the marking system was not independently tested in full and corrected scores are not comprehensively supplied. The evidence supports a bounded measure of grid-task performance; broader reasoning and intelligence claims remain unresolved.",
      "supported_claims": [
        "The tasks assess successful inference and application of rules through completed two-dimensional grids.",
        "The inspected software awards fractional problem credit when only some new inputs are solved.",
        "Human solving data informed construction and matching of test-set difficulty for people.",
        "Verified evaluations record settings and impose a spending limit, supporting comparisons within those conditions."
      ],
      "documented_problems": [
        "Post-release corrections addressed erroneous squares and unclear examples; affected AI scores are not all recalculated.",
        "Public evaluation problems are accessible, and the creators acknowledge possible exposure of hidden material.",
        "Verified evaluations use one run, and other evaluation routes may use different conditions.",
        "The software score and the dataset description's requirement for a fully solved problem use different units of success."
      ],
      "missing_information": [
        "Repeated identical evaluations and uncertainty estimates for AI scores.",
        "Systematic effects of instructions, grid presentation and software settings.",
        "Evidence excluding all unintended routes to high scores and establishing each system's exposure history.",
        "Evidence linking scores to language, social interaction, real-world work or broader intelligence.",
        "Independent verification of the complete marking system and complete checking of the reported public archive."
      ],
      "reinterpretations": [
        "For AI, a correct grid demonstrates successful output production, without identifying whether rule inference, search, prior exposure or another process produced it.",
        "Human-matched difficulty cannot be interpreted as AI-matched difficulty.",
        "A benchmark score represents an average of input success within problems, rather than necessarily the percentage of fully solved problems.",
        "Verified results describe performance under specified resource and system conditions, rather than an unrestricted measure of general intelligence."
      ],
      "closing_note": "Reports should clarify whether 'solved' means an input or an entire problem, and identify the version, exposure controls and evaluation route. The practical boundary between permitted development and discouraged evaluation-specific changes also needs clearer operational guidance."
    },
    {
      "benchmark": "designqa",
      "instrument_review": "DesignQA offers a practically grounded examination of finding and applying Formula SAE rules and interpreting selected vehicle materials. Practitioner contributions and additional review support relevance, but one rulebook, limited task types and uneven group sizes restrict coverage. Review exceptions and absent disagreement data leave answer quality incompletely established. Scoring combines text similarity and decision accuracy, so credit can reflect wording and formatting as well as engineering correctness. Equal weighting gives each group the same contribution despite differences in size and scoring; neither the combined score nor group scores are established as distinct underlying skills. Comparisons also reflect information supply because systems receive either the whole rulebook or retrieved passages. Reported variations in passages and images provide useful sensitivity evidence but do not establish repeatability under identical conditions. The small performance group makes fine rankings particularly fragile. Public materials permit partial inspection, while incomplete historical records limit reproduction. Scores therefore support task-specific comparisons under disclosed conditions, with insufficient evidence for broad engineering competence or confident interpretation of small differences.",
      "supported_claims": [
        "Questions address six types of work involving rules, terminology, components, dimensions and performance requirements.",
        "Real competition materials give the tasks a concrete connection to engineering practice.",
        "Reported results describe AI systems together with their supplied documents or retrieval arrangements.",
        "One additional correct answer changes accuracy in the 16-question performance group by 6.25 percentage points."
      ],
      "documented_problems": [
        "Question groups are highly unequal, while the overall score weights all six equally.",
        "Formatting and supplied-answer omissions can affect credit, including valid related rules missing from reference answers.",
        "All described scale-bar drawings comply, allowing an always-yes strategy to earn their decision credit; its use by tested systems is not established.",
        "Systems receive different information, complicating direct comparisons.",
        "Historical software, settings and inputs are not fully linked to every result, and one answer file has fewer rows than the paper's corresponding question count."
      ],
      "missing_information": [
        "Reviewer disagreement rates, remaining answer errors and comprehensive marking accuracy and consistency evidence.",
        "Repeated identical evaluations and uncertainty estimates sufficient to interpret small score differences.",
        "A baseline from human engineers and evidence of transfer to other documents or engineering projects.",
        "Established protected evaluation data, systematic overlap checks and clear training and repeated-submission rules.",
        "A clear record of revision effects, a located licence file and complete reuse guidance; their absence from inspected materials does not establish prohibited reuse."
      ],
      "reinterpretations": [
        "AI scores reflect engineering-task performance together with retrieval quality, presentation and response formatting.",
        "Text similarity is an operational scoring rule whose credit need not correspond directly to technical correctness.",
        "The overall score represents an equal-weight combination of heterogeneous task groups, not an established general engineering skill.",
        "Correct yes/no decisions on uniformly compliant drawings need not demonstrate checking or measurement ability."
      ],
      "closing_note": "Scoring instructions need to clarify acceptable alternative rules, equivalent wording and formatting, and the treatment of explanations. Reports should specify the exact inputs, information-supply method and scoring version used."
    }
  ]
}
